topic: The effects of formalized and trained non-reciprocal peer teaching on psychosocial, behavioral, pedagogical, and motor learning outcomes in physical education

sources.title: The effects of formalized and trained non-reciprocal peer teaching on psychosocial, behavioral, pedagogical, and motor learning outcomes in physical education
sources.authors: Whipp PR, Jackson B, Dimmock JA, Soh J.

findings.finding: Trained peer teachers facilitate better motor performance in their students compared to untrained peers.
findings.quote: the T-PT program significantly enhanced in-game performance actions and academic learning time among student recipients.

findings.finding: Formalized training enables peer teachers to provide more effective feedback and better-structured practice sessions.
findings.quote: Those in the T-PT also provided greater levels of feedback and structured learning time, as well as reporting more positive feelings about peer teaching

findings.finding: Structured support for teachers leads to a more positive learning environment with fewer obstacles for students.
findings.quote: fewer perceived barriers to accessing learning outcomes. These findings show that non-reciprocal peer-teachers who receive formalized support through training and tactical games approach-based teaching resources can enhance behavioral

principle: Providing peer teachers with formal training and structured resources significantly improves the motor performance and learning engagement of their students.
for_the_teacher: Provide learners with structured resources and clear pedagogical frameworks if they are asked to teach or demonstrate steps to others.
Ensure that peer-led practice sessions include specific, actionable feedback rather than just general observation.
Structure practice time clearly to maximize the amount of time students spend actively performing the movements.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study focused specifically on high school students in a physical education setting using a tactical games approach.
